# Faults

Every built-in fault. `provenance: vendor` reproduces a failure mode the vendor documents; `provenance: transport` is a transport-level failure mode no vendor documents. See [Chaos rules and faults](../concepts/chaos-rules-and-faults.md) and [Provenance labels](../concepts/provenance-labels.md).

| Fault | Scope | Provenance | Params | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate_limit` | request | vendor | retry_after_seconds | Reject the request as rate limited. |
| `server_error` | request | vendor |  | Fail the request with a vendor-shaped 5xx. |
| `unavailable` | request | vendor |  | Fail the request as temporarily unavailable. |
| `timeout` | request | vendor | delay_ms | Stall the request, then fail it. |
| `token_expiry` | request | vendor |  | Treat the caller token as expired mid-flow, without touching stored state. |
| `webhook.duplicate` | webhook | vendor | copies | Deliver the same event body more than once. |
| `webhook.delay` | webhook | vendor | delay_ms | Delay delivery. |
| `webhook.out_of_order` | webhook | vendor |  | Hold this event until the next one has been delivered. |
| `webhook.drop_ack` | webhook | vendor |  | Ignore a successful subscriber response so the retry schedule runs. |
| `webhook.drop` | webhook | vendor |  | Silently swallow the delivery: recorded as dropped, never sent to the subscriber. Filter with match.event_type. |
| `malformed_body` | request | transport | mode, status | Replace a successful response's body with something the vendor's own schema forbids. |
| `body_mutation` | request | transport | ops | Apply RFC 6901 JSON-pointer operations to a successful JSON response body, after the handler ran. |
| `connection_reset` | request | transport |  | Drop the connection after the response starts, before it completes. |
| `empty_response` | request | transport |  | Drop the connection as close to before any bytes as the binding can manage. |
| `slow_body` | request | transport | chunk_bytes, chunk_delay_ms | Stream a successful response body in chunks, with a delay between them. |
